summary.title: FIGARO: Controllable Music Generation Using Expert and Learned Features
summary.objective: To introduce a controllable symbolic music generation model that uses high-level, human-interpretable conditioning via description-to-sequence learning.
summary.problem: Current symbolic music generative models achieve high sample quality, but it remains difficult for users to control the output to match expectations because high-level, human-interpretable conditioning is lacking.
summary.methodology: Proposes description-to-sequence learning, which automatically extracts fine-grained, human-interpretable features (descriptions) from music and trains a sequence-to-sequence Transformer model to reconstruct the original sequence given only the description. Combines hand-crafted expert descriptions with learned representations via VQ-VAE.
summary.architecture: Transformer auto-encoder (4 encoder layers, 6 decoder layers) combined with a bar-level VQ-VAE for learned features and REMI+ input representation.
summary.results: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in multi-track symbolic music generation in terms of style transfer, sample quality, and adherence to input conditions, outperforming existing baselines in listening studies and objective metrics.
summary.limitations: Requires creative input in the form of a description rather than being fully unconditional; lacks explicit melody conditioning control.
summary.future_work: Training a prior model to generate descriptions unconditionally, adding new description functions (such as melody conditioning), and applying the description-to-sequence objective to other domains like natural language story generation.
